$schema_note: Local manufacturing knowledge base: material reference data, extending config/materials.json with planning-relevant fields (paintability, strength class, good_for tags). Not read by any print/upload code path.
extensibility_note: Additional materials (e.g. PC, PA/nylon, PVA support, carbon-fiber blends) can be added as new entries here without changing planner code - the decision engine reads whatever tags/fields are present.

pla.surface_finish_notes: Prints crisp fine detail well; low heat/impact resistance.
pla.notes: Good default for prototypes, signage, and indoor decorative parts. Low heat resistance.

pla_plus.surface_finish_notes: Similar print behavior and detail fidelity to standard PLA; slightly tougher.
pla_plus.notes: Slightly tougher than standard PLA, similar print behavior.

petg.surface_finish_notes: More flexible/impact-resistant than PLA; glossier finish, paint adhesion is generally poor without prep.
petg.notes: More flexible and impact-resistant than PLA; better for outdoor or functional parts.

abs.surface_finish_notes: Can be acetone vapor-smoothed; paints well after prep. Prone to warping without an enclosure.
abs.notes: Higher heat resistance; more prone to warping. Requires enclosure for best results.

asa.surface_finish_notes: Similar to ABS with better UV stability; paints well after prep.
asa.notes: UV-resistant alternative to ABS; a reasonable default for outdoor/exterior parts (e.g. plate frames).

tpu.surface_finish_notes: Flexible/rubbery finish; not a paint-friendly surface.
tpu.notes: Flexible filament; use for gaskets, grips, or flexible connectors only.

notes: Shrinkage/paintability/strength values are typical/reference figures, not guarantees for a specific spool, printer, or post-processing method.
Material choice also affects clearance tolerances; see config/tolerances.json.
good_for tags are used by the deterministic planning decision engine (factory.manufacturing.decision_engine) as keyword-adjacent hints only - not a substitute for human material selection.
